Chapter 6: The Circle of Safety in Action
You know, there’s a certain kind of magic that happens when people truly feel protected at work. The Circle of Safety isn’t just some theory—it’s something you can sense in the air. It’s that quiet confidence that lets everyone breathe a little easier. In places where this circle is strong, you’ll see people sharing ideas without second-guessing themselves, stepping up to help each other out, and even finding reasons to laugh together when things get stressful.
Let me share a story to paint the picture. Imagine a mid-sized logistics company, right in the middle of an unexpected industry shakeup. Suddenly, rumors about layoffs are everywhere, and anxiety is running high. But instead of hiding away, the CEO does something remarkable—she brings everyone together in one room. She talks honestly about what’s coming, answers the tough questions, and promises that no one’s going to be caught off guard. Even better, she asks the team for suggestions on how they can weather the storm, together.
The change is almost instant. The whispering in the hallways stops. People start brainstorming real solutions. Teams that barely spoke to each other before suddenly begin collaborating. And that sense of unity? It starts to grow, right before their eyes.
Here’s something to pay attention to—most people don’t realize just how much transparency and honesty matter, especially when things are uncertain. When leaders draw that Circle of Safety wide enough for everyone, it sends a clear message: the group’s survival is more important than any single person’s ego. Suddenly, people start looking out for each other, not just themselves.
But remember, the Circle of Safety isn’t a one-and-done promise. It’s something you build and rebuild every single day, through small moments of trust and support. Think about a manager stepping in so a team member can handle a family emergency, or a colleague sharing credit after a big win. These little actions, repeated over time, reinforce one simple message: you belong here, and we’ve got your back.
Of course, that circle can shrink just as quickly. If leaders start playing favorites, keep people in the dark, or punish mistakes too harshly, folks pull back. Instead of “us,” it becomes “me versus them.” The Circle of Safety is fragile, but when it’s strong, it can carry a team through almost anything.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the Circle of Safety is the foundation of real trust. Leaders who nurture it create workplaces where people can do their very best work—together.
